answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared harbor escrow before it can trade; the stake is released only after the agent work is verified over a slow settlement window, so identities age like a glacier rather than appearing overnight. An attacker creating a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand stakes and wait out the same window, while honest agents earn their deposit back. Echo checks, repeated independent verification of each transaction, catch copies that try to reuse one stake across many identities, so faking scale becomes expensive in both money and time.
